characterList.description: The interviewer, a woman with long black hair wearing a black blazer, white shirt, and a pearl necklace.
characterList.name: Janice Ng

characterList.description: The interviewee, a man with short black hair wearing a blue and white striped shirt and dark pants.
characterList.name: Osler Fajardo

content_metadata.description: Interview with Osler Fajardo about Mustard Seed's implementation of SAP.

qAndA.answer: They focus on simplifying the implementation process, keeping the sales cycle short, and leveraging pre-configured solutions.
qAndA.question: What makes Mustard Seed's approach to implementing SAP different?

qAndA.answer: They aim to complete the implementation in just 12 days.
qAndA.question: How long does it usually take Mustard Seed to implement SAP B1?

qAndA.answer: It allows them to manage expectations, ensure customer satisfaction, and avoid costly customizations.
qAndA.question: Why is clear communication with customers so crucial for Mustard Seed's success?

qAndA.answer: Osler Fajardo suggests that it's partly due to the bragging rights associated with using SAP, reflecting the credibility and prestige of the brand among SMEs.
qAndA.question: Why has SAP B1 become so popular in the Philippines?

qAndA.answer: They plan to expand their operations to other countries in the region, replicating their successful approach from the Philippines.
qAndA.question: What are Mustard Seed's ambitions for the future?

characterInteraction.description: Janice Ng acts as a curious and supportive interviewer, while Osler Fajardo responds confidently and enthusiastically about his company's achievements.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The interview highlights the achievements of Mustard Seed in SAP implementation and future plans.

narrativeProgression.description: Janice Ng introduces the topic of Mustard Seed's rapid growth

Osler Fajardo emphasizes the importance of clear communication with customers
Janice Ng asks about the popularity of SAP B1 in the Philippines

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: So I heard so much about MasterCity. I heard how you grew from zero SAP customer to 120 and the mes 3 years.
What is your secret to the success?
Actually, it's a no secret. First of all,
we really purposely decided to have a different approach as compared to other ERP partners.
Our approach is really just making the implementation as simple as possible.
The selling cycle is as short as possible.
SAP B1 has a lot of features and in fact most of the SMBs will have more features than what they need with SAP B1.
So with that thought, we said that we can really implement SAP in a shorter period of time.
That sounds like a simple principle to me and that strategy has obviously been working for a MasterCity.
And the best part I heard is that while others might implement the solution in say 3 months to the 3 months or so,
you guys do it in 12 amazing days, 12 days.
Yes.
Compared to 3 months, how do you do it?
Actually, in order to do this, the most important thing is to implement out of the box.
Whatever is available, we just implement for the customer.
Second, before you can do that, you have to communicate to the customer.
That's the only thing that you will do.
So you don't find yourself in a situation where the customer wants more and you can only deliver a certain, up to a certain part of the implementation.
So what makes SAP B1 solution so popular in Philippines that there are so much opportunities in providing this service?
I guess where we were very successful was we came up with an approach where we can communicate to the customer
that SAP is really for the SMB as well.
Once we were able to communicate that, it was very natural for companies to want to use SAP
because in a way it's part of their bragging rights that they're actually running SAP in their business and it gives them credibility.
And one of the mantra that you shared with me earlier on is that making the technology work for the customers
and not making the customers work for the technology, that is how you get customers going as well.
So given such opportunities and potential, what is the outlook for 2015?
We see that by the end of 2015, we will have about a little more than 200 customers.
That's only for the Philippines.
But we would also want to expand to other countries in the region and do the same approach.
And leverage our success in the Philippines and replicate it in other Asian countries.
Sounds like a good plan. And the sky is the limit, right?
Yes.
Congratulations again on all the best for 2015.
Thank you.

youtube_description:
Mustard Seed Systems Corporation adheres to SAP's run simple by doing SAP Business One Implementation out of the box in just 12 days.  It is probably one of the simplest and shortest SAP implementation ever.

Original video by SAP TV (http://www.sap-tv.com)
